transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, I ended up calling the EAP at work because... I don't know, lately every little bang in the office is just really getting to me. Like, if someone shuts a file drawer too loud or drops a coffee mug, I jump really hard. And then my chest just keeps racing for way longer than it should after something so small.
Have you experienced or witnessed a terrifying event that involved serious injury, death, or the threat of either?
No, not really. I mean, nothing like that. I haven't been in any bad accidents or seen anyone get hurt or anything. It's just... I don't know, it's just the loud noises that are getting to me lately.
Have you had sudden episodes of intense fear that come out of the blue, even when nothing specific is happening?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. It doesn't really happen for no reason. Like I said, it's pretty much just when there's a sudden noise or a loud bang at work that I get that racing feeling. I don't just get scared out of nowhere.
Do you find yourself avoiding places or situations because you might hear a sudden loud noise?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I still go into the office every day and do all my normal stuff. I haven't stopped going anywhere or avoided any specific places just because it might be loud. It's really just that when a noise does happen, it really catches me off guard.
When a sudden loud noise happens, do you feel that your reaction is much stronger than the actual danger warrants?

Yeah, definitely. I mean, that's actually what made me call EAP in the first place. It feels like every little bang in the office—like a file drawer shutting or someone dropping a coffee mug—just makes me jump really hard. And then my chest just keeps racing way longer than it should for something so harmless.
Do you feel afraid of loud noises themselves, even before one happens?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't really... sit around worrying that a noise is going to happen. It's not like I'm at my desk dreading it or feeling scared before anything even occurs. It's just that when the noise actually happens, that's when my body overreacts. But beforehand, I feel completely normal.
How long has this strong reaction to sudden loud noises been happening?
It's been going on for about two weeks now. Basically, it started right after this late-night confrontation I had with my regional boss.
Since the confrontation with your boss, have you been persistently worried or distressed about that event or your work situation?

No, not really. I mean, it wasn't a great night, but I'm not sitting around dwelling on it or stressing about my job. I don't feel distressed about going to work or anything like that. It's really just that physical jumpiness when a sudden noise happens. Mentally, I'm not worried about the situation itself.
How much have these reactions interfered with your work or daily activities?

Well, I'm still making it to work every day, so it hasn't stopped me completely. But... I guess it has slowed me down a bit. Like, I'm taking longer to get through my accounts and make staffing decisions. I've even had to ask my team to double-check some of the things I'd normally just handle on my own, just to be sure I'm not missing anything. It's frustrating, honestly. And with performance reviews coming up soon, I am a little worried that being slower or making silly mistakes could end up affecting my job.
Do you feel that your jumpiness began as a reaction to the confrontation with your boss?

I mean, I'm not really sure if it's a direct reaction to it. Like I said, I don't really feel stressed about the argument itself. But the timing definitely lines up... it started right after that night. So, maybe? I just don't know why my body would be reacting this way when I'm not really dwelling on what happened with him.
At the time it happened, did the confrontation with your boss feel emotionally upsetting or stressful to you?

No, honestly, it didn't. I mean, it was annoying, sure, but it wasn't like... emotionally devastating or anything. We got into it, he yelled, I stood my ground, and that was that. I didn't leave feeling traumatized or deeply upset. It was just a bad night at work. That's why this whole physical reaction thing is so confusing to me.
Around the time this jumpiness began, was there any other significant change or stressful event in your life besides the confrontation with your boss?

No, not really. Everything else has been pretty much the same. Just the usual day-to-day stuff at work and home. There wasn't any big change or other stressful event that happened around that time. It was just that one argument with my boss, and then this jumpiness started.
Have you recently increased your caffeine or energy-drink intake?

No, not at all. I mean, I have my regular cup of coffee in the morning, but I haven't added to that or anything. I don't really drink energy drinks, either. So, yeah, my caffeine intake is exactly the same as it's always been.
Do these exaggerated reactions to sudden noises happen only at work, or do they also happen in other places such as at home or in public?

It's mostly at work, honestly. That's actually what made me call the Employee Assistance Program. Every little bang in the office—like, if someone slams a file drawer shut, or drops a coffee mug—it just makes me jump so hard. And then my chest just keeps racing, way longer than it really should for something so small. It's really distracting.
When you are away from work, do sudden noises cause the same intense jumpiness and racing heart?

No, not really. I mean, if a car backfires or something loud happens when I'm out, I might startle a bit, but it's nothing like at work. At home, I feel pretty normal. It's just when I'm in the office that my nerves are completely shot.
When you think about your boss or the confrontation, do you notice the same intense jumpiness?

No, not jumpiness, really. I mean, thinking about him or what happened definitely makes my chest tight and my stomach kind of turn over, but I don't get that same startled, jumping out of my skin feeling unless there's an actual loud noise. It's more just... dread, I guess, when I think about him.
Before the confrontation with your boss, had you ever experienced this kind of jumpiness and prolonged racing heart in response to sudden noises?

No, never. Before that day with my boss, a loud noise was just a loud noise. I mean, I might have looked up if someone dropped something, but my heart didn't take off racing like it does now. This whole jumpy thing definitely only started after the confrontation.
